  "findings": [

      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Accidental gitlink/submodule added",
      "body": "The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (subproject commit) at the repository root. There is no `.gitmodules` entry or apparent use for it, so it looks like an accidental nested repository/submodule. This can break checkouts or tooling and should be removed before merge."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 137,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Substring query check can misclassify mixed or negated queries as error-only",
      "body": "`_is_error_focused_query` returns true whenever the raw query contains the substring `event.type:error`. This matches negated filters like `!event.type:error`, mixed queries like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and even tag/message text containing that substring. In those cases the endpoint rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()`, which can undercount or zero out non-error rows that do not have a meaningful `sample_weight`."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 135,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Upsampling decision ignores the actual executed query string",
      "body": "`_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET['query']`, but `_get_event_stats` can execute a different `query` argument, for example dashboard-split queries that append conditions such as `AND !event.type:transaction`. The upsampling decision should be based on the query actually being executed; otherwise transformed columns may be applied to a non-error query or omitted for an error-only split query."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 220,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of the dataset being queried",
      "body": "`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` because callers can execute the query with a different dataset, but the eligibility check passes the outer `dataset` variable. When the executed dataset differs, the decision may enable upsampling for the wrong dataset or fail to enable it for an error dataset. The check should use the dataset that will actually execute the query."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 112,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Upsampling is enabled for the errors dataset without corresponding tested aggregate registration",
      "body": "The helper returns true for `dataset == errors`, but the new `upsampled_count` aggregate is only added in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`. If the errors resolver does not inherit this function converter, allowlisted errors-dataset requests using `count()` will be rewritten to an unknown function and fail. This path is not covered by the tests."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py",
      "line": 1048,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "upsampled_count drops events with missing or null sample_weight",
      "body": "The aggregate is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. If any event in an allowlisted project has a missing/null `sample_weight` (old events, events without error-sampling context, malformed sample rates, etc.), that event contributes zero rather than one, silently undercounting errors. A default such as coalescing missing weights to 1, or an explicit guarantee that every row has a valid weight, is needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py",
      "line": 1047,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "toInt64 truncates fractional upsampled counts",
      "body": "`upsampled_count` casts `sum(sample_weight)` to Int64. If `sample_weight` can be fractional, which is likely for inverse sample rates, the result is truncated rather than rounded. This systematically biases estimated error counts downward. Return a numeric result or explicitly round if integer output is required."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py",
      "line": 1041,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function",
      "body": "The new SnQLFunction does not set `private=True`, unlike neighboring internal functions. API callers can request `upsampled_count()` directly, bypassing the allowlist/error-focused checks and potentially producing misleading weighted counts on data where upsampling should not apply. Mark the function private if it is only intended for internal column transformation."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 27,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Eligibility cache key uses a lossy Python hash and lacks effective invalidation",
      "body": "The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. This is not a collision-resistant identifier, and different project sets could theoretically share a key. In addition, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is not wired to allowlist changes and only deletes one exact project-set key, so allowlist updates can leave stale eligibility entries for up to 60 seconds. Use a deterministic digest or explicit key contents and provide real invalidation if needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 3554,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Tests miss unsafe upsampling paths",
      "body": "The new endpoint tests only cover simple `event.type:error` and `event.type:transaction` queries on discover. They do not cover negated or mixed queries, dataset=errors, topEvents, RPC paths, events missing `sample_weight`, or cache staleness. These are the paths most likely to expose wrong counts or query failures."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Accidental gitlink/submodule added
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (subproject commit) at the repository root. There is no `.gitmodules` entry or apparent use for it, so it looks like an accidental nested repository/submodule. This can break checkouts or tooling and should be removed before merge.

findings.title: Substring query check can misclassify mixed or negated queries as error-only
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns true whenever the raw query contains the substring `event.type:error`. This matches negated filters like `!event.type:error`, mixed queries like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and even tag/message text containing that substring. In those cases the endpoint rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()`, which can undercount or zero out non-error rows that do not have a meaningful `sample_weight`.

findings.title: Upsampling decision ignores the actual executed query string
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET['query']`, but `_get_event_stats` can execute a different `query` argument, for example dashboard-split queries that append conditions such as `AND !event.type:transaction`. The upsampling decision should be based on the query actually being executed; otherwise transformed columns may be applied to a non-error query or omitted for an error-only split query.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of the dataset being queried
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` because callers can execute the query with a different dataset, but the eligibility check passes the outer `dataset` variable. When the executed dataset differs, the decision may enable upsampling for the wrong dataset or fail to enable it for an error dataset. The check should use the dataset that will actually execute the query.

findings.title: Upsampling is enabled for the errors dataset without corresponding tested aggregate registration
findings.body: The helper returns true for `dataset == errors`, but the new `upsampled_count` aggregate is only added in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`. If the errors resolver does not inherit this function converter, allowlisted errors-dataset requests using `count()` will be rewritten to an unknown function and fail. This path is not covered by the tests.

findings.title: upsampled_count drops events with missing or null sample_weight
findings.body: The aggregate is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. If any event in an allowlisted project has a missing/null `sample_weight` (old events, events without error-sampling context, malformed sample rates, etc.), that event contributes zero rather than one, silently undercounting errors. A default such as coalescing missing weights to 1, or an explicit guarantee that every row has a valid weight, is needed.

findings.title: toInt64 truncates fractional upsampled counts
findings.body: `upsampled_count` casts `sum(sample_weight)` to Int64. If `sample_weight` can be fractional, which is likely for inverse sample rates, the result is truncated rather than rounded. This systematically biases estimated error counts downward. Return a numeric result or explicitly round if integer output is required.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function
findings.body: The new SnQLFunction does not set `private=True`, unlike neighboring internal functions. API callers can request `upsampled_count()` directly, bypassing the allowlist/error-focused checks and potentially producing misleading weighted counts on data where upsampling should not apply. Mark the function private if it is only intended for internal column transformation.

findings.title: Eligibility cache key uses a lossy Python hash and lacks effective invalidation
findings.body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. This is not a collision-resistant identifier, and different project sets could theoretically share a key. In addition, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is not wired to allowlist changes and only deletes one exact project-set key, so allowlist updates can leave stale eligibility entries for up to 60 seconds. Use a deterministic digest or explicit key contents and provide real invalidation if needed.

findings.title: Tests miss unsafe upsampling paths
findings.body: The new endpoint tests only cover simple `event.type:error` and `event.type:transaction` queries on discover. They do not cover negated or mixed queries, dataset=errors, topEvents, RPC paths, events missing `sample_weight`, or cache staleness. These are the paths most likely to expose wrong counts or query failures.
